sections.h2: What should a Muskegon seller expect from the city and county?
sections.html:
Muskegon sellers deal with a city that registers and inspects every rental, a lake-effect climate that is hard on roofs, and a county office that records deeds for a flat fee. A house that was ever a rental carries the most paperwork.

Census estimates put the city at 37,224 people for 2025, level with its 2020 base. Of 13,996 households, 53.1% own their home. Owned homes are valued at $142,300 at the median, rent is $996, and owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,064 a month. At those prices, a repair bill of a few thousand dollars takes a big bite out of a sale.

Median household income is $44,735, and 24.9% of residents live below the poverty line. Children make up 22.4% of the population and seniors 14.8%, only 15.5% of adults hold a four-year degree, and commutes average 20.6 minutes. Roughly 81% of residents stayed in the same house over the past year.

sections.h2: Where is Muskegon, and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Muskegon is the Muskegon County seat, a harbor city on the south shore of Muskegon Lake with Lake Michigan just beyond. Its 18.20 square miles include 4.05 of water, or 22.3%.

The Muskegon River enters the lake at the northeast end. Neighbors include North Muskegon, Muskegon Township, Fruitport Township, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores, and Grand Rapids lies 42 miles to the southeast. Lumber drew settlers beginning in 1837, which earned the city nicknames such as Lumber Queen of the World, and Bluffton, once its own lumber village, was annexed in 1889.

  • Downtown: about two miles of lakefront with hotels, a 25,000-square-foot convention center completed in 2021 and the Trinity Health Arena.
  • Schools: Muskegon Public Schools dates to 1860, and Muskegon Community College and Baker College are in the area.
  • Travel: I-96, US 31, M-46 and M-120 serve the city, MATS runs buses and trolleys, and the Lake Express car ferry crosses to Milwaukee.
  • Flights: Muskegon County Airport has nonstop service to Chicago O'Hare.

The waterfront is a draw. The Saturday farmers market in summer welcomes more than 10,000 visitors, boutique shops fill Western Avenue, and trolley stops include the USS Silversides and Muskegon State Park. In May 2022 local groups announced that cleanup work on Muskegon Lake was finished, which began the EPA's review of removing the lake from its list of Areas of Concern. The city runs under a seven-member commission and a hired city manager.

Snow is the main wear factor. A year brings 87.2 inches, with January alone at 29.1 inches, and 48 days with measurable snow, mostly lake-effect. Roofs, gutters and furnaces take that punishment, and an inspector on the buyer's side will start there.

sections.h2: Which Muskegon rental rules follow a house into a sale?
sections.html:
Every rental in the city must be registered and inspected, and the certificate stays with the owner who earned it. Anyone buying with a rental plan starts fresh, with a new certificate and a new inspection.

A clean first inspection earns a 6-year certificate, while violations put the property on a 3-year cycle. Because the city works under the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, rentals need carbon monoxide readers, and a licensed contractor must certify the furnace and water heater at 0 ppm in the breathable area. An owner who lives more than 30 miles off must name a responsible party within 30 miles.

sections.h2: Does a Muskegon short-term rental license go with the house?
sections.html:
Usually not. Licenses issued after the ordinance was adopted cannot be transferred, so the registration stays with the owner who obtained it.

One exception exists for properties with an active short-term rental status before March 2024. They may make a one-time status transfer in any zone using a signed formal document, and the new owner still completes registration and inspections. The overlay district has 11 zones with caps ranging from 13 in Zone 11 to 95 in Zone 9, and Zone 1, Beachwood and Bluffton, is full with a waitlist. Properties inside the downtown authority, the Lakeside Business Improvement District and the Lakeside Corridor Improvement Authority fall outside the caps.

A single-family short-term rental pays $500 a year, with each added unit adding another $500. Any buyer whose offer rests on vacation-rental income should read the overlay rules before signing.

sections.h2: What are the Muskegon tax deadlines at closing?
sections.html:
The city bills in two rounds. Summer bills issue July 1 and are due September 14, and winter bills issue December 1 and are due February 14.

Summer taxes left unpaid collect 1% interest monthly once past due and a 3% penalty if still open on February 14, while winter taxes take a 3% penalty after their due date. Whatever the city has not collected by February 28 becomes delinquent on March 1 and the County Treasurer collects it. Your title company will prorate the current bill at the closing table.

The buyer's taxable value is reset the year after the sale (MCL 211.27a), which can lift the next bill well above yours. If you claimed the principal residence exemption, rescind it within 90 days of moving out or face $5 a day, up to $200 (MCL 211.7cc).

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Muskegon County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
One flat charge applies: $30 per deed, mortgage or other instrument, however many pages.

  • Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments with a warranty clause first need a $5 certificate from the County Treasurer's Office.
  • Real estate record copies run $1 a page, plus $5 per certification.
  • Combined transfer tax is $4.30 per $500 of price, so a $150,000 sale pays $1,290.
  • A free Fraud Guard alert emails you whenever your name appears on a recorded document.

Gifts between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild are exempt from state transfer tax (MCL 207.526).

sections.h2: How should I choose a way to sell in Muskegon?
sections.html:
The choices are a listing, a sale by owner or a cash purchase. Weigh repair costs, carrying costs and timing against price, because a lower-priced house can lose a bigger share of its value to fixes.

Before you talk to buyers, gather:

  • The rental certificate and latest furnace and water heater inspection, if the house was rented
  • The latest summer and winter tax bills, so the closing agent can settle what is owed
  • Records of roof, gutter and basement work after a lake-effect winter
  • Your deed or land contract paperwork

For a cash price, send us the Muskegon address and the house's condition. We buy as-is, so a failed rental inspection or a winter-damaged roof need not be fixed first.

faqs.q: Will my Muskegon rental certificate pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Rental certificates do not transfer to new owners, so a buyer opens a new certificate, passes an inspection and pays the registration fee. Mention that early if your buyer plans to rent the house out.

faqs.q: How long does a Muskegon rental certificate last?
faqs.a: Six years after a clean first inspection and three years when violations are found. The yearly registration fee keeps it in good standing between inspections.

faqs.q: When do unpaid Muskegon taxes go to the county?
faqs.a: March 1. The city passes along anything uncollected by February 28, and the County Treasurer takes over from there.

faqs.q: What would transfer tax be on a $150,000 Muskegon sale?
faqs.a: $1,290, made up of $1,125 state tax and $165 county tax.

faqs.q: What does a Muskegon short-term rental registration cost?
faqs.a: $500 a year for a single-family unit, rising to $1,000 for a duplex and $2,500 for a quinplex. Reinspections start at $100 and climb in $100 steps.
